## p155: Asgard's return to Poti

**Sources on this page:** p155 A1, p155 A2.

<a id="edition-cases-context-p155-p155-asgards-return-to-poti"></a>



Asgard is expected at Poti to collect troops. The same message reports that
Asgard and Tresivolus arrived at the sender's port on 7 November and asks for
acknowledgment. The port is not named in the ciphertext. Hopman's diary
places the two ships at Sevastopol on that date, with orders to return to
Poti; its spelling *Tresivolos* differs from the telegram's `TRESIVOLUS`.
[Diary passages and source references](../../data/reviews/hopman_context.json).

<a id="edition-cases-context-p155-source-supported-wording"></a>

#### Source-supported wording

A1 already supplies **ASGARD** from complete observed pairs. A2 has both a
complete occurrence and `A?GARD`; the repeated name supports the S fill.
Three other telegrams provide the vocabulary in their raw readings:

| Proposed wording | Independent observed wording | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `VORAUSSICHTLICH` | `RUECKUNFT VORAUSSICHTLICH 0100` | [p182 B](182.md#edition-cases-radio-return-time-and-vehicle-attempt-p182-b) |
| `BEFINDLICHE` | `BEFINDLICHEN TRUPPEN` | [p222 A2](222.md#edition-cases-military-liman-troop-reports-a2-special-requirements-and-acknowledgment) |
| `EMPFANG BESTAETIGEN` | `EMPFANGBESTAETIGEN` | [p129 A8](129.md#edition-cases-military-transylvania-situation-report-p129-a8) |

These witnesses establish vocabulary used elsewhere in the collection.
They are not copies of this telegram. The [completion certificate](../../experiments/p155_shipping_completion/certificates.json)
records every observed pair in the cited words and in the repeated name.

<a id="edition-cases-context-p155-coordinate-costs-and-tied-gap-placements"></a>

#### Coordinate costs and tied gap placements

All source indices are zero-based. In A1, source 97 `G`→`A` and source 118
`X`→`G` repair `IO?AUSSICHTLICH` and `BEFINDLBCHE`; source 88, printed `C`,
is filled with `D` to supply R in `VORAUSSICHTLICH`.

For A2, the completed body requires source 174 `V`→`A`, source 175 `A`→`D`,
and fills at the two printed dashes: 177→`X`, 178→`D`. The final repair has
two equivalent source accounts:

| Added coordinate before source | Added value | Further observed substitution |
| ---: | :---: | --- |
| 183 | `A` | Source 183 `D`→`X` |
| 184 | `X` | Source 183 `D`→`A` |

Each produces the same 186-coordinate witness with 3 observed substitutions,
2 printed-mask fills and 1 added-slot fill. Pricing this fixed body at all
186 gap positions gives exactly these two minima. The earlier raw variants
at 183, 185, 184 and 0 remain in the original certificate; the new comparison
is conditional on the proposed body.

<a id="edition-cases-context-p155-consequence-for-p73"></a>

### Consequence for p73

This message follows the same radio route as p73 and was received five
minutes later, but the origin dates differ. p73 has an 26 October heading
and `0911 (26)`; p155 has `2035 (7)`. Reception-time proximity therefore
does not establish a common original-date key. The [p73 source-context record](../../data/reviews/p73_source_context.json)
retains the dating evidence and the unsuccessful search for an 25–27 October
companion.

## p155 B — Von Schorlemer cannot currently be released from the administrative staff

**Edition context:** Von Schorlemer: demobilization work inquiry and reply.

**Related source pages:** [p122 B](122.md#source-p122-b).

<a id="edition-cases-people-schorlemer-demobilization-inquiry-von-schorlemer-demobilization-work-inquiry-and-reply"></a>



**Source review and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

A clear-address request on p122 and an encrypted reply on p155 form a source-linked exchange about von Schorlemer's availability for demobilization work. The earlier request asks whether he can be released to the Trade Ministry; the later administrative-staff reply says he cannot currently be spared. Both native frames and every repair remain explicit. The later reply supports the name and topic; the 33 supplied mask values in the first request remain editorial proposals.

<a id="source-p155-b"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-people-schorlemer-demobilization-inquiry-p155-b"></a>

### p155 B

**Source transcription — header:** `B) LP v NKJ (7.09 p.m., November 7th); 0800 VON UKS (7/11); RICHI-160`

**Readable German:** based on the explicitly repaired output below.

> Handelsminister Berlin. Oblt. v. Schorlemer z. Zeit hier nicht abkoemmlich. OKM Verw. Stab.

**Meaning:** The administrative staff informs the Trade Minister in Berlin that First Lieutenant von Schorlemer cannot currently be released.

**Unresolved details and editorial limits.**

- The source visibly prints four dashes. The 160-slot native frame is unchanged.
- The name repair SCKORLEMER to SCHORLEMER is supported by the independent clear p122 B address, not by a guessed biography. No first name or unique historical person is supplied.
- The exchange concerns availability for duty; it does not itself establish that a reassignment or recall actually occurred.

### Evidence and credit

Published period keys: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and George Lasry (2017 key list). Earlier unreviewed repository candidates are retained separately. Source review and explicit editorial work: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.

The certificates replay every coordinate alteration, compare the independent column/domain reconstruction with the cipher implementation, and re-encrypt every complete edited output. For a partial output, an injective global completion of the square and residual source masks supplies an explicitly nonhistorical round-trip witness. Each readable passage preserves every nonseparator output label; literal protected fields are also checked without removing their internal separators. Source crops are bound to the original PDF by page, rectangle, scale, file digest and RGB-pixel digest.

Reproduce with `python experiments/schorlemer_demobilization_inquiry/verify.py --verify`. Add `--pdf /path/to/adfgvx-childs.pdf` to regenerate and compare the delivered source pixels.

A round-trip proves compatibility with a stated reading. Editorial spelling repairs remain proposals, and literal number labels are not automatically historical dates, quantities or reference numbers.

## Request to repeat an unreadable eighth part

**Sources on this page:** p155 C1, p155 C2.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov7-eighth-part-repetition-request-to-repeat-an-unreadable-eighth-part"></a>



**Source review and conditional edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Childs p155 C is a two-part request to check and repeat an earlier eighth part that could not be deciphered. The second part reads directly under the published Nov7–9 key. The first part prints a six-coordinate group where its advertised length requires five; its body is shown under explicitly priced one-coordinate exclusions. The original earlier eighth part is not supplied or solved by this request.

[Reviewed source](../../experiments/nov7_eighth_part_repetition/sources/p155_C.png) · [Exact inputs](../../experiments/nov7_eighth_part_repetition/inputs.json) · [All alternatives and joint witnesses](../../experiments/nov7_eighth_part_repetition/certificates.json)

**Source transcription — header:** `C) NKJ v LP (6.42 a.m., November 8th); FUER COS 2240 (7/11), 2 TLE; 1 TL RICHI-186; 2 TL RICHI-136`.

<a id="source-p155-c1"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov7-eighth-part-repetition-p155-c1"></a>

### p155 C1

**Conditional frame.** The literal source has 187 slots, including the six-slot group `VGVXAA`, three noncoordinate glyphs (`H`, `S`, `H`), and no printed dash. The advertised length is 186. The displayed example excludes the observed `G` at source index 61, then masks the three invalid glyphs. Excluding an observed coordinate is a separate frame operation; it is not a zero-cost OCR correction. Other exclusions are retained below.

**Readable German — conditional interpretation**, after that one exclusion and two explicitly recorded source-mask fills:

> Da achter Teil des AL?CHIS 2?X10, Leitstelle 707 POT Nr. 1002 an Sektion Politik Berlin nicht zu entziffern,

**Meaning:** The eighth part of a message identified by the literal token AL?CHIS and the date-like field 2?X10 cannot be deciphered. The routing names Sektion Politik Berlin. The sentence continues in C2.

`AL?CHIS`, the date-like field `2?X10`, and the station/reference labels remain literal. The primary pair `707 / 1002` is one example, not a uniquely recovered identification.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov7-eighth-part-repetition-conditional-digit-reading"></a>

### Conditional digit reading

The [shared Nov7–9 digit interpretation](../../experiments/nov7_9_joint_digits/README.md) reads **25.10** in part 1 and **RM 5 Nr. 153303** in part 2. The opposite square gives 26.10 and RM 6 Nr. 163303. The first part’s `AL?CHIS` field remains unresolved, and the retained source-frame alternatives are unchanged.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov7-eighth-part-repetition-the-overlong-group-does-not-determine-unique-reference-labels"></a>

### The overlong group does not determine unique reference labels

All six choices of one excluded coordinate inside the literal `VGVXAA` group are preserved. Each costs one observed-coordinate exclusion. The table records the further word substitutions and source-mask fills needed for the common readable body.

| Excluded source index | Printed coordinate | Station / reference labels | Additional observed substitutions | Source-mask fills |
| ---: | --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| 60 | V | `727 / 1002` | 0 | 2 |
| 61 | G | `707 / 1002` | 0 | 2 |
| 62 | V | `707 / 1022` | 0 | 2 |
| 63 | X | `707 / 1022` | 1 | 2 |
| 64 | A | `707 / 1022` | 2 | 2 |
| 65 | A | `707 / 1022` | 2 | 2 |

The first three choices produce different correlated numerical fields with the same repair price. The final two choices delete one of the adjacent As and produce the same frame, but their source indices remain distinct. A plausible duplicated A is not silently treated as the historically correct deletion. Conversely, the cheaper language repair does not prove that the excluded G was a transmitted error.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov7-eighth-part-repetition-one-shared-unresolved-cell-three-fields"></a>

### One shared unresolved cell, three fields

The unknown in `2?X10` and both unknowns in `RMX?NRX1?3303` all decode from **the same square cell `XA`**. They cannot be chosen independently. Under the published pair of unused labels `{5, 6}`, the two complete shared assignments are:

| XA label | First-part date-like field | Second-part reference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `5` | `25X10` | `RMX5NRX153303` |
| `6` | `26X10` | `RMX6NRX163303` |

The other unknown cell receives the remaining label, preserving injectivity. Both assignments have joint full round-trip witnesses for both message parts under every recorded exclusion. These demonstrate compatibility; neither assignment is selected as an authenticated historical date or reference. The separate `AL?CHIS` character remains source-mask uncertainty and is not resolved by this equality alone.

## p155 D — Morning report: derailed freight train and both tracks blocked

**Edition context:** Gomel route derailment and station-train forwarding.

**Related source pages:** [p169 B](169.md#source-p169-b).

<a id="edition-cases-military-nov7-derailment-and-trains-gomel-route-derailment-and-station-train-forwarding"></a>



**Source review and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Two source editions concern railway operations: a freight-train derailment blocking both tracks on the proposed Gomel–Bachmatsch route, and a message about forwarding a station train and construction train to Group Winterfeld. The wagon count, train labels, abbreviations and office references remain literal.

<a id="edition-cases-military-nov7-derailment-and-trains-p155-d-1"></a>

### p155 D

**Source transcription — header:** `D) NKJ v LP (3.55 p.m., November 7th); FUER UKS 1355; RICHI-316`

**Readable German:** based on the explicitly repaired output below.

> OK Mackensen. Morgenmeldung vom 7X11X18: Auf Strecke Gomel, Bachmatsch entgleiste ein Gueterzug. 2? Wagen zertruemmert. Beide Gleise sind gesperrt. Hrgr. Kiew RMX1XAX7097X18.

**Meaning:** A morning report addressed to Oberkommando Mackensen says a freight train derailed on the proposed Gomel–Bachmatsch route, that a quantity written 2? of wagons was wrecked, and that both tracks are blocked. The unresolved wagon-count label and final reference remain literal.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output** — every native source slot in printed order, under the stated published key.

```text
OKXMACKENSENXXMORGENMELDUNGVOM7X11X18AUFSTRECKEXGOMELXBNCHMABSCH?ENBGLEISTEEI?GUETERZUG?2?WAGENZE?TRUEMMERT?BEIDEGLEISESINDGESPERRTXXHRGRXKIEWXRMX1XAX7097X18X
```

**Edited output** — 3 observed-coordinate substitutions and 5 source-mask fills; no coordinate inserted, deleted or moved.

```text
OKXMACKENSENXXMORGENMELDUNGVOM7X11X18AUFSTRECKEXGOMELXBACHMATSCHXENTGLEISTEEINGUETERZUGX2?WAGENZERTRUEMMERTXBEIDEGLEISESINDGESPERRTXXHRGRXKIEWXRMX1XAX7097X18X
```

</details>

**Unresolved details and editorial limits.**

- The source has four dashes and a literal Y-shaped noncoordinate glyph in DXYVF. These five slots are masked before decoding and filled separately in the proposed reading.
- The place repair BNCHMABSCH to BACHMATSCH requires two observed-coordinate substitutions; the other substitution changes ENBGLEISTE to ENTGLEISTE. This is an explicit word proposal, not a new external geographical identification.
- The unknown in 2? is the globally unresolved XA cell, whose domain is {5,6} in the published Nov7–9 square. This edition does not choose 25 or 26 wagons.
- Correct source groups FVXDD and VXDVG each have five slots. Earlier OCR strings with repeated X coordinates are not treated as source evidence.

<a id="edition-cases-military-nov7-derailment-and-trains-conditional-shared-digits"></a>

### Conditional shared digits

The [Siegfried reference comparison](../../experiments/nov7_9_joint_digits/README.md) supplies one shared conditional assignment, XA=5 and VF=6, to both railway records.

<a id="source-p155-d"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-military-nov7-derailment-and-trains-p155-d"></a>

#### p155 D

**Readable German — conditional shared digits, with the existing source edition retained:**

> OK Mackensen. Morgenmeldung vom 7.11.18: Auf Strecke Gomel, Bachmatsch entgleiste ein Gueterzug. 25 Wagen zertruemmert. Beide Gleise sind gesperrt. Hrgr. Kiew. RM 1 A 7097 18.

Under the shared-reference assignment XA=5, the original pair at source 294/56 gives **25 wagons**, completing **158/158** labels. The opposite assignment gives 26. The earlier three observed substitutions and five mask fills are unchanged.

### Coupled wagon and train labels

The unresolved symbols are linked by the unchanged Nov7–9 square. All indices below are zero-based plaintext positions.

| Square cell | Source occurrences | Shared constraint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| XA | p155 D position 89; p169 B position 47 | The unknown in wagon label `2?` is the same label as the unknown in train label `S11?2`. |
| VF | p169 B positions 107, 108 and 110 | All three unknowns in `1B1??1?` are the same label, and differ from XA. |

VF and XA carry the two remaining labels `{5, 6}` bijectively. There are therefore two global assignments, not five independent numerical guesses. Neither assignment is established as the historical numbering.

<a id="edition-cases-military-nov7-derailment-and-trains-evidence-and-credit"></a>

### Evidence and credit

Published period keys: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and George Lasry (2017 key list). Earlier unreviewed repository candidates are retained separately. Source review and explicit editorial work: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.

The certificates replay every coordinate alteration, compare the independent column/domain reconstruction with the cipher implementation, and re-encrypt every complete edited output. For a partial output, an injective global completion of the square and residual source masks supplies an explicitly nonhistorical round-trip witness. Each readable passage preserves every nonseparator output label; literal protected fields are also checked without removing their internal separators. Source crops are bound to the original PDF by page, rectangle, scale, file digest and RGB-pixel digest.

Reproduce with `python experiments/nov7_derailment_and_trains/verify.py --verify`. Add `--pdf /path/to/adfgvx-childs.pdf` to regenerate and compare the delivered source pixels.

A round-trip proves compatibility with a stated reading. Editorial spelling repairs remain proposals, and literal number labels are not automatically historical dates, quantities or reference numbers.
